title: This Bird Flies 10,000 Miles and Barely Flaps Its Wings
subject: wandering albatross

scenes.text: A bird crosses an ocean and barely flaps its wings.
The wandering albatross has the widest wingspan of any living bird, about 3.5 meters.
GPS tracking shows single trips of about 10,000 miles over open sea.
The trick is dynamic soaring. It climbs into the wind, turns, then dives toward the waves.
Wind is slower near the water and faster higher up, and the bird steals energy from that difference.
It works in winds above about 18 miles an hour, common in the Southern Ocean. So it flies on the wind, not on muscle.

description:
A bird crosses an ocean and barely flaps its wings.
The wandering albatross uses dynamic soaring to cover about 10,000 miles on a single trip.
Could you fly that far on borrowed wind?
